panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Chest HRCT from a child in a case series of X-linked hyper-IgM syndrome, showing pulmonary infection/infiltrates and hilar lymphadenopathy; included as a respiratory-infection manifestation, though the specific pathogen is T. marneffei and the imaging pattern is not specific. B: Chest HRCT from a child with X-linked hyper-IgM syndrome showing bilateral ground-glass opacities as a pulmonary infection/infiltrative manifestation; the caption does not identify a specific pathogen or a specific hyper-IgM finding beyond pulmonary involvement.

From a pulmonary imaging perspective, four patients developed lymphadenopathy and diffuse infiltration with T. marneffei infection on high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) (Fig. 1A). The other three patients (P2, P3, and P4) showed ground-glass opacities on HRCT (Fig. 1B). Specifically, seven patients were followed up for 3–10 years. During the follow-up period, only P3 died of respiratory failure.P4 undertook hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), and quite a good recovery of hemopoiesis was observed 6 months after HSCT.
